portion_doctrine: Segments 1-10 are 80% boilerplate video transcript (timestamps + speech fragmentation). The core content is a mashup of three talks: (1) seven AI skills for creators (infographic builder, diagram generator, decision-making expansion, steelman reasoning, consensus AI models, skill finder), (2) startup pitch framework (market + team + pain + progress, NOT AI buzzwords), and (3) one-person AI business systems (using ChatGPT for founder-opportunity fit, automation, no-code tools). Genuine gold is sparse but actionable: skills-not-AI-models philosophy, founder-fit ideation, pitch structure, content automation. Noise includes heavy timestamps, video UI markers, applause indicators, and repetitive speech patterns.
operating_rules: In a world with equal AI access, skills determine output quality and differentiation, not the models themselves
When pitching to investors or customers, pitch the market size, team, pain, and progress - NOT the AI. AI is secondary checkbox, not the vehicle
Just because an idea has AI in it does not make it category-winning - build tools that get better as AI improves, not static AI features
Product discovery: measure feature usage before and after launch via instrumentation, call users who drop off mid-flow to diagnose UX friction directly
Discoverability of features via UI is a first principle: an undiscovered feature does not count as shipping; most engineering orgs fail on this
Content creation focus: story > authenticity myth - humans care about narrative density, information value, entertainment, and self-interest, not whether creator is real or AI
Entry barrier to creation dissolves with agentic tools: future advantage shifts to uniqueness, narrative, and brand differentiation, not technical capability
For one-person founders: proof-of-concept in days via no-code, then spend majority of first 30 days on positioning, ICP definition, and proprietary data strategy
prompts: I'm trying to come up with a one-person business idea. Ask me as many questions as you need about my skill set before giving me suggestions. (ChatGPT ideation interview)
When designing UX: ask AI to design interface leveraging best practices as if designed by Apple/Airbnb, wireframe solution before building
For feature validation: screenshot competing products and upload to GPT with direction: 'Use these examples to guide your design; I like the white space and interaction here'
Pitch structure template: market size, team strength, domain experience, pain clarity, traction proof. Say AI as passing mention only
tools: Infographic Builder skill - builds interactive HTML infographics with tooltips, animations, responsive layouts
Excalidraw diagram generator - creates flowcharts, process diagrams, technical architecture visuals as downloadable SVG
Expand and Contrast skill - complexifies or simplifies ideas via guided question prompts; helps scope definitions
Steelman skill - pressure-tests assumptions and ideas via adversarial reasoning (spots competing solutions, ICP gaps, feature validity)
Swarm Consensus skill - queries multiple AI models (Grock, Gemini, ChatGPT) in one call via OpenRouter API, summarizes agreement
Find Skills skill - queries skills.sh database (90,000+ community skills) to avoid rebuilding from scratch
ChatGPT for founder-opportunity interview - automated ideation via question prompts
Cursor IDE - preferred web coding tool for proof-of-concept builds
Open Router API - multi-model consensus queries
skills: B-roll indexing and search (indexing video footage for quick retrieval)
gates: Feature discoverability gate: measure usage before deploy, call users who abandon mid-flow
AI pitch gate: never lead with AI; filter through market/team/pain/progress first
Authenticity deflation gate: user behavior shows story and density trump 'realness' - AI content can win if better delivery
Proof-of-concept gate: days to build, weeks to position - skip months of overbuilding
content_ideas: Seven AI skills for one-person teams (automation hierarchy)
How to pitch AI startups without sounding like every other AI startup
AI avatars and generated content win when narrative/story density beats traditional production
One-person business operating system: tools + positioning + proprietary data strategy in first 30 days
Why product management is now the bottleneck (engineers build features faster than PMs can validate them)
B-roll search automation saves editors 15 hours per week per person
contradictions: Authenticity paradox: emphasis on 'people want real you' undermined by data showing AI-generated content succeeds on story and density alone; Dan's own observation that he didn't notice three influencer avatars were AI until revealed
weird_gold: Turbo B-roll: internal tool that indexes 60TB of video footage and enables natural-language search (e.g., 'Dan and Renee hugging') saving 15 hours per editor per week
Neo tool: AI version of personal brain - everything someone has ever said indexed and learned, only on that person's actual words, paired with AI avatar to auto-generate content
Three confirmed AI influencers with million+ followers that Dan didn't recognize as AI until told directly - validates AI avatar distribution viability
Genie 3: AI real-time scene generation for video (announced last week in transcript context)
